source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use occupied-bed technique, turning the client safely from side to side","B":"Postpone linen changes until the client can get out of bed independently","C":"Remove all linens first and leave the client uncovered during replacement","D":"Ask the immobile client to stand briefly while the linens are replaced"}}
source_row.rationale: For a client unable to get out of bed, the nurse uses the occupied bed-making technique, working from one side of the bed to the other, safely rolling the client (with assistance as needed) while maintaining the client's privacy, safety, comfort, and proper body mechanics for the nurse throughout the process.
source_row.source_detail: Occupied-bed checklist and safe linen-change technique for a client who remains in bed; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Assistant: Making an Occupied Bed
source_row.stem: A nurse needs to change the bed linens for a client who is unable to get out of bed. The nurse should use which technique?
